Unstructured reports need deterministic preparation before AI extraction.

• Long PDFs
• Multi-column layout
• Tables, headings, lists, faculty names
• Inconsistent formats
• Not machine-readable

• Token overflow
• Missed data
• Hallucination
• Department mixing
• Expensive processing

Use a deterministic multi-stage pipeline
where each stage produces a
standardised output for the next stage.
The goal is not just extraction — the goal is traceable, validated, reusable institutional data.
Strict stage contracts keep the pipeline auditable and team-safe.
Each stage has a strict input, strict output, and fixed file location. This prevents team members from overwriting each other’s work.
Raw PDF → Blocks → Target Blocks → Semantic HTML → Metrics JSON → Validated Profile

Dossier Schema: The Rulebook for AI Extraction
Person A defines what the system must extract.

• Metric definitions
• Required fields
• Allowed categories
• Currency formats
• Faculty classifications
• Ranking indicators
• Responsible research assessment indicators

A fixed structure makes stage ownership and file contracts explicit.

Simple rules keep the four-person team synchronized.
01 Every stage reads only from the previous stage.
02 Every stage writes only to its assigned output folder.
06 AI output must be validated before final use.
07 Low-confidence entries go to human review.
08 Team members do not overwrite another module.
10 Every final metric links back to source page or section.
Governance is what keeps the four-person team synchronised.
